subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should OpenClaw classify and react to plain provider messages like `LLM error api_error: Internal server error` in cron fallback chains, especially for shared auth-profile cooldowns, fast-fail behavior, retry/backoff, and delivery alerts?
rationale: The choice changes provider failover, cron retry semantics, failure notification behavior, and shared auth-profile cooldown safety, so automation should not choose the permanent policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Cron-local server_error
options.body: Classify the cron-visible run error as retryable `server_error` and prove fast-fail/retry/alert behavior without marking shared auth-profile health for ambiguous plain text.

options.title: Shared provider cooldown
options.body: Treat plain API internal-server failures as provider outage signals that can skip same-provider candidates across runs, accepting broader cooldown effects.

options.title: Keep timeout-only with proof
options.body: Leave plain provider 500 text as timeout-like only if focused cron/fallback tests prove it fails before the outer deadline and notifies operators.

recommendation.title: Cron-local server_error
recommendation.body: Classify the cron-visible run error as retryable `server_error` and prove fast-fail/retry/alert behavior without marking shared auth-profile health for ambiguous plain text.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available owner signal for the cron/failover policy boundary from current-main blame and prior related review context.
